data.name: InvalidExpression
data.value: Invalid expression '{{{{{0}}}}}'.
data.comment: {0} is the text between the double braces. The doubled braces are escapes that print as {{ and }}.

data.name: DuplicateRequestName
data.value: Duplicate request name '{0}' on lines {1} and {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} and {2} are the request-line numbers of the two requests.

data.name: InvalidHeader
data.value: Invalid header '{0}' (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the start of the header line, up to the first whitespace, ':' or '=' and cut after 32 characters. The rest of the line is left out because it can hold a secret. {1} is the line number.

data.name: InvalidRequestName
data.value: Invalid request name '{0}' (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the start of the first token after @name, up to the first ':' or '=' and cut after 32 characters, or empty when there is no token. {1} is the line number.

data.name: InvalidVariableDefinition
data.value: Invalid variable definition '{0}' (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the start of the variable line, up to the first whitespace, ':' or '=' and cut after 32 characters. The rest of the line is left out because it can hold a secret. {1} is the line number.

data.name: MessageAtLine
data.comment: {0} is an error message without its final period. {1} is the line number it applies to.

data.name: UnknownHttpMethod
data.value: Unknown HTTP method '{0}' (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the start of the request line, up to the first whitespace, ':' or '=' and cut after 32 characters. The rest of the line is left out because a URL can hold a key. {1} is the line number.

data.name: DotEnvVariableNotDefined
data.value: '{0}' is not defined in {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the name given to $dotenv. {1} is the path of the .env file that was read.

data.name: DotEnvFileNotFound
data.value: '{0}' cannot be read with $dotenv: file {1} was not found.
data.comment: {0} is the name given to $dotenv. {1} is the path where the .env file was looked for. $dotenv is literal syntax and is not translated.

data.name: DynamicVariableOffsetOutOfRange
data.value: Offset '{1} {2}' for '${0}' is out of range.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $. {1} is the offset amount and {2} its unit. The resulting date is outside the supported range.

data.name: EnvironmentVariableNotSet
data.value: Environment variable '{0}' is not set.
data.comment: {0} is the name given to $processEnv.

data.name: InvalidDynamicVariableArguments
data.value: Invalid arguments for '${0}'. Expected '{{{{{1}}}}}'.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $. {1} is its full syntax, such as $randomInt [min max]. The doubled braces are escapes that print as {{ and }}.

data.name: InvalidDynamicVariableDateFormat
data.value: Invalid date format '{1}' for '${0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $. {1} is the custom .NET date and time format string.

data.name: InvalidDynamicVariableInteger
data.value: Invalid integer '{1}' for '${0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $. {1} is the argument that is not a 32-bit integer.

data.name: InvalidDynamicVariableOffset
data.value: Invalid offset '{1} {2}' for '${0}'. Expected an integer and one of ms, s, m, h, d, w, M, y.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $. {1} is the offset amount and {2} its unit. The unit list is case-sensitive syntax and is not translated.

data.name: InvalidDynamicVariableRange
data.value: Invalid range for '${0}': min {1} is greater than max {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $. {1} and {2} are the min and max arguments as written.

data.name: UnknownDynamicVariable
data.value: Unknown dynamic variable '${0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the dynamic variable name without its $.

data.name: EnvironmentFileNotFound
data.value: --env {0} was given but no http-client.env.json was found above {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the environment name given to --env. {1} is the path of the .http file. --env and http-client.env.json are literal names and are not translated.

data.name: EnvironmentFileNotObject
data.value: Environment file {0} must contain a JSON object.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the environment file or of its .user file.

data.name: EnvironmentNotFound
data.value: Environment '{0}' not found in {1}. Available: {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the environment name given to --env. {1} is the path of the environment file. {2} is the comma-separated list of the environments that are defined.

data.name: EnvironmentNotFoundNoneDefined
data.value: Environment '{0}' not found in {1}, which defines no environments.
data.comment: {0} is the environment name given to --env. {1} is the path of the environment file.

data.name: EnvironmentUnsupportedValue
data.value: Environment '{0}' in {1} has an unsupported value.
data.comment: {0} is the environment name, which is not a JSON object. {1} is the path of the environment file or of its .user file.

data.name: EnvironmentVariableUnsupportedValue
data.value: Variable '{0}' in {1} has an unsupported value.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the path of the environment file or of its .user file. The value is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: InvalidEnvironmentFile
data.value: Environment file {0} is not valid JSON.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the environment file or of its .user file. Used when the error has no line number, as for a repeated property name. The file content is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: InvalidEnvironmentFileJson
data.value: Environment file {0} is not valid JSON (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the path of the environment file or of its .user file. {1} is the line number of the error. The file content is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: MultipleProjectFiles
data.value: More than one project file was found in {0}.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the folder that holds several .csproj files.

data.name: UnknownSecretProvider
data.value: Variable '{0}' uses unknown provider '{1}'. Supported: {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the provider name as written in the environment file. {2} is the comma-separated list of supported provider names, which are not translated.

data.name: SecretFieldMissing
data.value: Variable '{0}' ({1}) is missing '{2}'.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the provider name. {2} is the name of the required JSON property that is absent, empty or not a string.

data.name: SecretFieldInvalid
data.value: Variable '{0}' ({1}) has an invalid '{2}'. Expected a string that is not blank.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the provider name. {2} is the name of the optional JSON property that is present but blank or not a string. A string in the wrong shape has its own message. The value is left out.

data.name: EntraAccessTokenInvalidScope
data.value: Variable '{0}' (EntraAccessToken) has an invalid 'scope'. Expected a single scope made of letters, digits and . - : _ / (for example api://my-api/.default).
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. scope is a literal JSON property name and is not translated. The value is left out because it would be printed to the terminal as written.

data.name: EntraAccessTokenInvalidTenantId
data.value: Variable '{0}' (EntraAccessToken) has an invalid 'tenantId'. Expected a tenant ID (GUID) or a domain name.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. tenantId is a literal JSON property name and is not translated. The value is left out because it would be printed to the terminal as written.

data.name: EntraAccessTokenFailed
data.value: Variable '{0}' (EntraAccessToken): could not get an access token.{5} scope: {1}{5} tenant: {2}{5} tried: {3}{5} fix: {4}
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the scope. {2} is the tenant ID, or the EntraAccessTokenDefaultTenant text. {3} is the message of the credential failure. {4} is the command that fixes it. {5} is the line break. The labels are padded so the values line up; keep the two leading spaces and the alignment.

data.name: EntraAccessTokenDefaultTenant
data.value: default
data.comment: Shown on the tenant line of EntraAccessTokenFailed when the variable names no tenant.

data.name: KeyVaultInvalidResourceId
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AzureKeyVault): 'resourceId' does not end with a valid vault name.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. resourceId is a literal JSON property name and is not translated.

data.name: KeyVaultSecretNotFound
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AzureKeyVault): secret '{2}' was not found in vault '{1}' (404).
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the vault name. {2} is the secret name.

data.name: KeyVaultForbidden
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AzureKeyVault): access to secret '{2}' in vault '{1}' was forbidden (403). Check that your account can read secrets in this vault.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the vault name. {2} is the secret name.

data.name: KeyVaultRequestFailed
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AzureKeyVault): could not read secret '{2}' from vault '{1}' (HTTP {3}).
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the vault name. {2} is the secret name. {3} is the HTTP status code. The service's own message is left out.

data.name: KeyVaultUnreachable
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AzureKeyVault): could not reach vault '{1}' to read secret '{2}'. Check the vault name in 'resourceId' and your network connection.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the vault name. {2} is the secret name. Used when the request got no HTTP response. resourceId is a literal JSON property name and is not translated.

data.name: KeyVaultSignInFailed
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AzureKeyVault): could not sign in to read secret '{2}' from vault '{1}'.{4} tried: {3}{4} fix: az login
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the vault name. {2} is the secret name. {3} is the message of the credential failure. {4} is the line break. az login is a command and is not translated. The layout matches EntraAccessTokenFailed, without the scope and tenant lines because the provider takes neither; keep the two leading spaces and the alignment.

data.name: UserSecretsNoProject
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): no project file was found in {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the folder of the environment file, which holds no .csproj file.

data.name: UserSecretsNoUserSecretsId
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): project file {1} has no UserSecretsId.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the path of the .csproj file. UserSecretsId is a literal MSBuild property name and is not translated.

data.name: UserSecretsInvalidUserSecretsId
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): project file {1} has an invalid UserSecretsId.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the path of the .csproj file. Used when the ID holds characters that are not allowed in a folder name. UserSecretsId is a literal MSBuild property name and is not translated.

data.name: UserSecretsInvalidProject
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): project file {1} is not valid XML.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the path of the .csproj file.

data.name: UserSecretsFileNotFound
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): user secrets file {1} was not found.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the path of the secrets.json file.

data.name: UserSecretsInvalidFile
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): user secrets file {1} is not a valid JSON object.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the path of the secrets.json file. The file content is left out because it holds secrets.

data.name: UserSecretsSecretNotFound
data.value: Variable '{0}' (AspnetUserSecrets): secret '{1}' was not found in {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the secret name given by secretName. {2} is the path of the secrets.json file.

data.name: EncryptedWindowsOnly
data.value: Variable '{0}' uses the Encrypted (DPAPI) provider, which only works on Windows.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. Encrypted is the provider name and is not translated.

data.name: EncryptedInvalidBase64
data.value: Variable '{0}' (Encrypted): 'value' is not valid base64.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. value is a literal JSON property name and is not translated. The value itself is left out.

data.name: EncryptedCannotDecrypt
data.value: Variable '{0}' (Encrypted): 'value' could not be decrypted. A DPAPI value only works for the Windows user and machine that encrypted it.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. value is a literal JSON property name and is not translated. The value itself is left out.

data.name: ReferenceNoContentAtPath
data.value: The named request does not contain any content at this path '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is the reference expression, such as login.response.body.$.token. The wording matches Visual Studio's HTTP0028 error.

data.name: ReferenceBodyNotJson
data.value: '{0}' {1} body is not JSON.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} is the literal keyword request or response from the reference and is not translated. The body is left out because it may hold secrets.

data.name: ReferenceBodyDuplicateProperties
data.value: '{0}' {1} body has a JSON object with a repeated property name, which a JSONPath cannot read.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} is the literal keyword request or response from the reference and is not translated. The body is left out because it may hold secrets.

data.name: ReferenceBodyInvalidUnicode
data.value: '{0}' {1} body has JSON text that is not valid Unicode.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} is the literal keyword request or response from the reference and is not translated. Used when a JSON string holds an escaped surrogate without its pair. The body is left out because it may hold secrets.

data.name: ReferenceInvalidJsonPath
data.value: Invalid JSONPath '{0}' in '{1}'.
data.comment: {0} is the JSONPath. {1} is the whole reference expression. Also used when a filter function in the path fails, for example on a regular expression that is not valid.

data.name: ReferenceBodyNotDecoded
data.value: '{0}' response body is in Content-Encoding {1}, which is not decoded, so it cannot be referenced.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} is the list of content codings the tool does not decode, such as br, and is not translated. Content-Encoding is a header name and is not translated.

data.name: ReferenceBodyNotXml
data.value: '{0}' {1} body is not well-formed XML. A body with a DOCTYPE is not supported.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} is the literal keyword request or response from the reference and is not translated. The body is left out because it may hold secrets.

data.name: ReferenceInvalidXPath
data.value: Invalid XPath '{0}' in '{1}'. Namespace prefixes, variables and XSLT functions are not supported.
data.comment: {0} is the XPath. {1} is the whole reference expression. XSLT is a name and is not translated.

data.name: ReferenceXPathMultipleNodes
data.value: XPath '{0}' matched {1} nodes; expected one.
data.comment: {0} is the XPath. {1} is the number of matched nodes, always two or more.

data.name: ReferenceHeaderNotFound
data.value: '{0}' {1} has no '{2}' header.
data.comment: {0} is the request name. {1} is the literal keyword request or response from the reference and is not translated. {2} is the header name.

data.name: ReferenceAllHeadersUnsupported
data.value: '{0}' is not supported. Name one header, as in 'headers.Content-Type'.
data.comment: {0} is the reference expression, which ends in headers.*. headers.Content-Type is literal syntax and is not translated.

data.name: ReferenceUnsupportedBodySelector
data.value: '{0}' is not supported. After 'body.' use '*', a JSONPath starting with '$' or an XPath starting with '/'.
data.comment: {0} is the reference expression. body. is literal syntax and is not translated.

data.name: VariableNotDefined
data.value: Variable '{0}' is not defined (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the line number of the expression that uses it.

data.name: VariableNotDefinedNoEnvironment
data.value: Variable '{0}' is not defined (line {1}). No environment selected; available: {2}. Pass --env <name>.
data.comment: {0} is the variable name. {1} is the line number of the expression that uses it. {2} is the comma-separated list of the environments that are defined. --env is a literal option name and is not translated.

data.name: UrlNotAbsolute
data.value: '{0}' is not an absolute http or https URL (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the URL after variable substitution, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {1} is the line number of the request line.

data.name: RequestNotSent
data.value: Request '{0}' has not been sent.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a request that a reference reads before the request was sent.

data.name: RequestNotFound
data.value: Request '{0}' referenced on line {1} does not exist.
data.comment: {0} is the request name used in a reference. {1} is the line number of the reference.

data.name: RequestDependencyCycle
data.value: Request dependency cycle: {0}.
data.comment: {0} is the request names of the cycle joined with ' -> ', starting and ending with the same name.

data.name: ContentHeaderWithoutBody
data.value: Header '{0}' ignored: a request without a body cannot have content headers (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the header name, such as Content-Type. {1} is the line number of the header. A warning; the wording follows Visual Studio's HTTP0009. The header value is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: DroppedContentType
data.value: Content-Type on line {0} not sent: the request has no body.
data.comment: {0} is the line number of the Content-Type header. A line of the verbose log, not a warning. The header value is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: HeaderNotSendable
data.value: Header '{0}' is not a valid HTTP header and cannot be sent (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the header name. {1} is the line number of the header. The header value is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: HeaderValueHasLineBreak
data.value: Header '{0}' has a value that contains a line break and cannot be sent (line {1}).
data.comment: {0} is the header name. {1} is the line number of the header. Also used for a null character in the value. The header value is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: GraphQLQueryMissing
data.value: The GraphQL request on line {0} has no query and cannot be sent.
data.comment: {0} is the line number of the request line. GraphQL is a product name and is not translated. The body is left out because it can hold a secret.

data.name: GraphQLVariablesNotObject
data.value: The GraphQL variables of the request on line {0} are not a JSON object; the request cannot be sent.
data.comment: {0} is the line number of the request line. Used when no text after a blank line of the body is a JSON object and the text after a blank line starts as one does: a brace, then a quote or the closing brace. GraphQL and JSON are not translated. The variables are left out because they can hold a secret.

data.name: UnsupportedHttpVersion
data.value: '{0}' is not a supported HTTP version. Use HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 or HTTP/3.
data.comment: {0} is the version written at the end of the request line, such as HTTP/9. HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are literal syntax and are not translated.

data.name: SendFailed
data.value: Could not send {0} {1}: {2}
data.comment: {0} is the HTTP method. {1} is the URL, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {2} is the message of the network failure, which ends with its own punctuation.

data.name: SendFailedCertificateNotTrusted
data.value: Could not send {0} {1}: {2} The server certificate was not trusted. Pass --insecure to skip certificate validation.
data.comment: {0} is the HTTP method. {1} is the URL, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {2} is the message of the TLS failure, which ends with its own punctuation. --insecure is a literal option name and is not translated.

data.name: Redirected
data.value: Redirected to {0} ({1})
data.comment: {0} is the URL a redirect leads to, as the server sent it; provider-resolved values are shown as *** when the URL takes parts of the request URL. {1} is the status code of the redirect, such as 302. Written to standard error once for each redirect that is followed.

data.name: SendTimedOut
data.value: {0} {1} timed out after {2} s.
data.comment: {0} is the HTTP method. {1} is the URL, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {2} is the timeout in seconds; s is the unit symbol.

data.name: ResponseNotDecoded
data.value: The response to {0} {1} is left encoded: Content-Encoding {2} is not decoded, only gzip and deflate are.
data.comment: {0} is the HTTP method. {1} is the URL, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {2} is the list of content codings the tool does not decode, such as br. Content-Encoding is a header name; gzip and deflate are coding names; none of them are translated. A warning, shown after "warning: ".

data.name: ResponseNotValidCoding
data.value: Could not decode the response to {0} {1} ({2}): the body is not valid {3} data.
data.comment: {0} is the HTTP method. {1} is the URL, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {2} is the status code, such as 200. {3} is the content coding that failed, such as gzip, and is not translated.

data.name: ResponseDecodedTooLarge
data.value: Could not decode the response to {0} {1} ({2}): the {3} body is larger than {4} MiB when decoded.
data.comment: {0} is the HTTP method. {1} is the URL, with provider-resolved values shown as ***. {2} is the status code, such as 200. {3} is the content coding, such as gzip, and is not translated. {4} is the limit in mebibytes; MiB is the unit symbol.

data.name: BinaryBodySummary
data.value: (binary body, {0}, {1}; use --show body to write it)
data.comment: {0} is the body size with its unit, such as 1.5 KB. {1} is the Content-Type value of the response. Shown in place of a body that is not text. --show body is a literal option with its value and is not translated.

data.name: BinaryBodySummaryNoContentType
data.value: (binary body, {0}; use --show body to write it)
data.comment: {0} is the body size with its unit, such as 1.5 KB. Used when the response has no Content-Type. --show body is a literal option with its value and is not translated.

data.name: OutputError
data.value: error: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the error message, which ends with its own punctuation.

data.name: OutputFileWarning
data.comment: The canonical file(line): warning: message form of compiler and MSBuild output; keep the punctuation. {0} is the path of the .http file as given, {1} the line number, {2} the warning message, which ends with its own punctuation. "warning" is not translated.

data.name: OutputWarning
data.value: warning: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the warning message, which ends with its own punctuation.

data.name: OutputVerbose
data.value: verbose: {0}
data.comment: {0} is a line of the --verbose log. The prefix tells the log apart from warnings and errors on standard error.

data.name: VerboseHttpFile
data.value: HTTP file: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the full path of the .http file that is read.

data.name: VerboseEnvironmentFile
data.value: Environment file: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the full path of the http-client.env.json file that was found. http-client.env.json is a file name and is not translated.

data.name: VerboseEnvironmentUserFile
data.value: Environment user file: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the full path of the http-client.env.json.user file that is read next to the environment file. The file name is not translated.

data.name: VerboseDotEnvFile
data.value: .env file: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the full path of the .env file that $dotenv reads. .env and $dotenv are literal names and are not translated. The values in the file are never shown.

data.name: VerboseNoEnvironmentFile
data.value: Environment file: none
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log, written when no http-client.env.json file was found.

data.name: VerboseEnvironment
data.value: Environment: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the environment chosen with --env.

data.name: VerboseNoEnvironment
data.value: Environment: none
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log, written when no environment was chosen with --env.

data.name: VerbosePlan
data.value: Plan: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the list of requests in the order they are sent, the selected request last, each by its name or title, or by its method and URL as written in the file.

data.name: VerboseExchange
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log for each request sent. {0} is the HTTP method, {1} the URL with provider-resolved values shown as ***, {2} the status code and reason phrase of the response, such as 200 OK, and {3} the time in milliseconds. ms is the unit symbol.

data.name: VerboseDecoded
data.value: Decoded: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the list of content codings, such as gzip, that the response body was decoded from.

data.name: VerboseToken
data.value: Token for {0}: tenant {1}, expires {2}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log for each access token acquired. The token itself is never shown. {0} is the scope, {1} the tenant ID the token was issued by, {2} the expiry time in UTC.

data.name: VerboseTokenTenantUnknown
data.value: unknown
data.comment: Stands for {1} of VerboseToken when the tenant cannot be read from the token.

data.name: VerboseCredentialSelected
data.value: Credential: {0}
data.comment: A line of the --verbose log. {0} is the type name of the Azure credential that supplied the token, such as AzureCliCredential, and is not translated.

data.name: CommandDescription
data.value: Runs a request from a Visual Studio .http file.
data.comment: The description of the tool at the top of the --help output. .http is a file extension and is not translated.

data.name: FileArgumentDescription
data.value: The .http or .rest file that holds the request.
data.comment: The --help description of the file argument. .http and .rest are file extensions and are not translated.

data.name: NameOptionDescription
data.value: The request to run, as named by '# @name <name>' or titled by '### <title>' in the file.
data.comment: The --help description of --name. # @name and ### are literal .http syntax and is not translated.

data.name: ListOptionDescription
data.value: Prints the name, else the title, of each request that --name can select, one per line in file order, and sends nothing. Warns about the requests it leaves out.
data.comment: The --help description of --list. --name is a literal option name and is not translated. In the third person, like the other option descriptions that start with a verb.

data.name: ListRequestWithoutName
data.value: Request has no name or title.
data.comment: Warning from --list about a request it leaves out, shown after the file and line.

data.name: ListTitleSharedWithOne
data.value: Title '{0}' is also used at line {1}.
data.comment: Warning from --list, shown after the file and line of a request it leaves out because one other request has the same title. {0} is the title, compared ignoring case. {1} is the line number of the other request.

data.name: ListTitleSharedWithMany
data.value: Title '{0}' is also used at lines {1}.
data.comment: Warning from --list, shown after the file and line of a request it leaves out because other requests have the same title. {0} is the title, compared ignoring case. {1} is the comma-separated list of the line numbers of the other requests.

data.name: ListTitleIsAName
data.value: Title '{0}' is the name of the request at line {1}.
data.comment: Warning from --list about a request it leaves out, shown after the file and line. {0} is the title. {1} is the line number of the request whose # @name is that title.

data.name: ListOptionWithName
data.value: --list can't be used with --name.
data.comment: --list and --name are literal option names and are not translated. Shown when both are given.

data.name: EnvOptionDescription
data.value: The environment in http-client.env.json to take variables from.
data.comment: The --help description of --env. http-client.env.json is a file name and is not translated.

data.name: VerboseOptionDescription
data.value: Logs what the tool does to standard error: files read, requests sent, tokens acquired (never their value).
data.comment: The --help description of --verbose.

data.name: ShowOptionDescription
data.value: What to print: full (the request with secrets masked, then the status, headers and formatted body as received), headers (status line and response headers), status (status line only), or body (the response body with gzip and deflate decoded, control characters not neutralised). Default: full in a terminal, body when the output is piped or redirected.
data.comment: The --help description of --show. full, headers, status and body are literal option values and are not translated.

data.name: InsecureOptionDescription
data.value: Skips server certificate validation.
data.comment: The --help description of --insecure. In the third person, like the other option descriptions that start with a verb.

data.name: VarOptionDescription
data.value: Sets a variable for this run, over the file and the environment. Can be repeated. Values are not masked; for a secret, use a secret provider in the environment file.
data.comment: The --help description of --var.

data.name: VarOptionInvalid
data.value: --var '{0}' is not name=value.
data.comment: --var is a literal option name and is not translated. {0} is the text of the --var argument before its first '=', which is not a valid variable name. The text after the '=' is never shown because it can be a secret.

data.name: VarOptionNeedsNameValue
data.value: --var needs name=value.
data.comment: --var is a literal option name and is not translated. Shown when a --var has no argument, or its argument has no '=' or nothing before it. The argument is not shown because it can be a secret.

data.name: VarOptionNotUsed
data.value: --var '{0}' is not used in {1}; variable names are case-sensitive.
data.comment: --var is a literal option name and is not translated. {0} is the variable name given to --var, which no {{name}} in the file refers to. {1} is the path of the .http file. The value is never shown because it can be a secret.

data.name: FileNotFound
data.value: File '{0}' was not found.
data.comment: {0} is the path given on the command line, which does not exist or is a folder.

data.name: UnrecognizedOption
data.value: Unrecognized option '{0}'.
data.comment: {0} is a command-line token that starts with '-', stands where the file is expected and names no file.

data.name: FileExtensionNotSupported
data.value: File '{0}' must have the extension .http or .rest.
data.comment: {0} is the path given on the command line. .http and .rest are file extensions and are not translated.

data.name: FileReadFailed
data.value: Could not read a file: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the operating system's message for the failed read, which names the path and ends with its own punctuation. The file content is never part of it.

data.name: RequestNameNotFound
data.value: No request named or titled '{0}' in {1}. Names and titles: {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the name given to --name. {1} is the path of the .http file. {2} is the comma-separated list of the request names and the ### titles in the file.

data.name: RequestNameNotFoundNoneNamed
data.value: No request named or titled '{0}' in {1}, which has no named or titled requests.
data.comment: {0} is the name given to --name. {1} is the path of the .http file. A title is the text after ### on the separator line above a request.

data.name: RequestTitleAmbiguous
data.value: More than one request is titled '{0}' (lines {1}). Give one a '# @name'.
data.comment: {0} is the name given to --name, which matches the title of more than one request. {1} is the comma-separated list of the line numbers of those requests. # @name is literal and is not translated.

data.name: MultipleRequestsNoName
data.value: {0} has {1} requests; pick one with --name. Names and titles: {2}. A request with neither a name nor a title can't be picked from a script; add '# @name <name>' or '### <title>' above it.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the .http file. {1} is the number of requests, always two or more. {2} is the comma-separated list of request names and ### titles. --name, # @name and ### are literal and are not translated.

data.name: MultipleRequestsNoneNamed
data.value: {0} has {1} requests and none has a name or title; add '# @name <name>' or '### <title>' above one and pick it with --name.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the .http file. {1} is the number of requests, always two or more. --name, # @name and ### are literal and are not translated.

data.name: NoRequests
data.value: {0} has no requests.
data.comment: {0} is the path of the .http file.

data.name: NoRequestSelected
data.value: No request was selected.
data.comment: Shown when the interactive request picker is closed without a choice.

data.name: DependencyFailed
data.value: Dependency '{0}' returned {1}; '{2}' was not sent.
data.comment: {0} is the name of the request that was sent first. {1} is its status code and reason phrase, such as 404 Not Found. {2} is the name of the selected request, else its ### title, else its method and URL as written in the file. ### is literal and is not translated.

data.name: Cancelled
data.value: Cancelled.
data.comment: Shown after 'error: ' when the run is stopped with Ctrl+C.

data.name: UnexpectedError
data.value: Unexpected {0}: {1}
data.comment: Shown after 'error: ' for a failure the tool did not foresee. {0} is the .NET exception type name. {1} is the exception message, or for an AggregateException the comma-separated type names of the exceptions it holds.

data.name: WrongTenantHint
data.value: The token is for another tenant. Set "tenantId" on the EntraAccessToken variable, or run with AZURE_TOKEN_CREDENTIALS=AzureCliCredential to use only the Azure CLI's sign-in.
data.comment: Shown after a 401 response with InvalidAuthenticationTokenTenant to a request that used an EntraAccessToken variable. "tenantId" is the name of a field in the environment file and EntraAccessToken is a provider name; AZURE_TOKEN_CREDENTIALS=AzureCliCredential is an environment variable setting, and AzureCliCredential is a credential name; none of these are translated.

data.name: PickerTitle
data.value: Select a request to run
data.comment: The title of the interactive request picker. Square brackets are not allowed here.
